answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a licensed radio beacon whose site a spectrum regulator records. A verifier checks the beacon across a ridge between two receivers, accepting only site-matched attenuation, so duplicates need separate licenses. An expired license transfer counts as a relic requiring a fresh operator check. Enforced rule: one active beacon per identity-checked operator, so n extra identities cost n licenses and n period fees. With per-identity reward at most R, profit is n(R-C), positive only while R>C; regulator collusion remains a weakness.
